props.label: About Us
props.heading: Spaces designed around how you actually live
props.body:
Raavee Kitchen and Interior offers bespoke design and remodelling solutions, blending aesthetic elegance with everyday functionality.

We specialise in modular kitchens and custom interiors, crafting personalised spaces tailored to your lifestyle. Our designs feature smart storage solutions, premium finishes and ergonomic layouts designed to maximise your home's potential.

A kitchen is the room you use most and forgive least. We plan the working triangle, the height of the counter and the position of every drawer around the person who will actually cook in it — because a kitchen that photographs well and works badly is a failure you live with for fifteen years.

Come to the studio at Manewada Square with your floor plan, or send it on WhatsApp, and we will talk through what is possible before anything is quoted.

pillars.title: Made to your plan
pillars.text: Every unit is built to your measurements, not adjusted from a standard size and filled with a gap.

pillars.title: Smart storage
pillars.text: Corner pull-outs, tall units and drawer inserts planned around what you actually store.

pillars.title: Premium finishes
pillars.text: Laminate, acrylic and PU finishes with the wear and cleaning trade-offs of each explained honestly.

pillars.title: Ergonomic layouts
pillars.text: Counter and unit heights set to the person who cooks, not a catalogue default.

props.label: Layouts
props.heading: Kitchen and wardrobe layouts
props.sub: The configurations we build most often. Which one suits you depends on the room — send us the plan and we will tell you.

items.title: L-Shaped Kitchen
items.desc: Two adjacent runs of counter. The most efficient layout for a small to medium kitchen and the one we build most often.

items.title: Parallel Kitchen
items.desc: Two facing runs with a walkway between. Excellent for narrow kitchens and for two people working at once.

items.title: Island Kitchen
items.desc: A free-standing central unit adding counter, storage and a place to sit. Needs the floor area to carry it — we will tell you honestly if yours does not.

items.title: Walk-in Wardrobe
items.desc: A dressing area with open and glass-fronted storage, planned around what you own rather than a standard rail-and-shelf split.

items.title: Sliding Wardrobe
items.desc: Sliding shutters where a hinged door has nowhere to open into — the usual answer in a compact bedroom.

items.title: TV & Crockery Units
items.desc: Living and dining storage built to match the kitchen, with cable management and lighting planned in rather than added after.

items.q: How long does a modular kitchen take?
items.a: Typically four to six weeks from final drawing approval to installation, depending on the finish and the hardware. Site measurement and design come before that. We give you a date at the time of the order rather than a vague estimate.

It depends on the size, the finish and the hardware, so we quote after measuring rather than giving a figure that changes later. Bring or send your floor plan and we will give you a written quotation with the specification itemised.

Laminate is the most durable for the money and the easiest to live with. Acrylic gives a high gloss but shows fingerprints. PU gives the best paint finish but costs more and is harder to repair locally. We will talk through the trade-offs for your usage rather than pushing the expensive one.
Yes, with our own team. That matters more than it sounds — when the manufacturer and the fitter are different companies, any problem becomes an argument between them with you in the middle.

items.q: Can you remodel my existing kitchen?
items.a: Yes. Sometimes the carcass is sound and only the shutters, hardware and counter need replacing, which costs far less than a full rebuild. We will tell you which situation you are in after seeing it.

items.q: Do you work on offices as well as homes?
items.a: Yes — workstations, storage, reception counters and cabin furniture for offices and clinics, using the same modular approach.

items.q: What do you need from me to start?
items.a: A floor plan with measurements, or an appointment for us to measure. Then a conversation about how you cook, what you store and who uses the space. Everything else follows from that.
